Read and remember the taxonomic backbone

Source: R/read.R
WFO.read.Rd

WFO.read() reads the backbone file. WFO.remember() remembers where the file is and loads it, so that later sessions need neither the path nor a new download.

Usage

WFO.read(
  WFO.file = NULL,
  select = NULL,
  core.only = FALSE,
  as.data.frame = FALSE
)

read_classification(
  path = file.path("wfo_data", "classification.csv"),
  select = NULL,
  core.only = FALSE,
  as_data_frame = FALSE
)

WFO.remember(WFO.file = NULL, WFO.data = "WFO.data", WFO.pos = 1, ...)

Arguments

WFO.file, path

Path to the backbone (classification.csv or classification.txt), or a directory that contains it. For WFO.read() and WFO.remember(), NULL uses the remembered location, or, if that file no longer exists, the newest release in the data folder (see WFO.releases()).

select

Names of columns to read (saves time and memory).

core.only

If TRUE, read only the columns used by this package: taxonID, scientificName, scientificNameAuthorship, taxonRank, taxonomicStatus, nomenclaturalStatus, acceptedNameUsageID, family, genus, specificEpithet, verbatimTaxonRank and infraspecificEpithet. Ignored if select is given.

as.data.frame, as_data_frame

If TRUE, return a data.frame instead of a data.table.

WFO.data

Name of the object created by WFO.remember().

WFO.pos

Environment position for that object, as argument pos of assign() (1: the global environment).

...

Further arguments for WFO.read(), such as core.only.

Value

WFO.read(): a data.table (or data.frame). WFO.remember(): the path of the backbone (invisibly); the backbone is assigned to WFO.data.

Details

WFO.read() uses data.table::fread(). All columns are read as character, so that identifiers such as "wfo-0000000001" and codes such as "NA" are never changed or turned into missing values. The separator is detected (the WFO file is tab-separated despite its extension). Selected columns that are not in the file are skipped with a warning.

WFO.remember() saves the location in the user configuration directory (tools::R_user_dir()); a location saved by WorldFlora is also found. With WFO.file = NULL, the matching functions use the remembered backbone too, or, if it no longer exists, the newest release in the data folder of WFO.download(). A message gives the file and the release used.

read_classification() is deprecated: use WFO.read(). It used the argument names of the stand-alone download script, unlike the other functions.

See also

WFO.download(), WFO.releases()

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
data(WFO.example2026)
data.table::fwrite(WFO.example2026, f, sep = "\t")
bb <- WFO.read(f, core.only = TRUE)
str(bb)
#> Classes ‘data.table’ and 'data.frame':	48 obs. of  12 variables:
#>  $ taxonID                 : chr  "wfo-4100000110" "wfo-1200070526" "wfo-4000034168" "wfo-7000000046" ...
#>  $ scientificName          : chr  "Palmae" "Reinwardtia" "Saurauia" "Arecaceae" ...
#>  $ scientificNameAuthorship: chr  "Juss." "Blume ex Nees" "Willd." "Bercht. & J.Presl" ...
#>  $ taxonRank               : chr  "family" "genus" "genus" "family" ...
#>  $ taxonomicStatus         : chr  "Synonym" "Synonym" "Accepted" "Accepted" ...
#>  $ nomenclaturalStatus     : chr  "" "" "Conserved" "Valid" ...
#>  $ acceptedNameUsageID     : chr  "wfo-7000000046" "wfo-4000034168" "" "" ...
#>  $ family                  : chr  "" "Actinidiaceae" "Actinidiaceae" "Arecaceae" ...
#>  $ genus                   : chr  "" "Reinwardtia" "Saurauia" "" ...
#>  $ specificEpithet         : chr  "" "" "" "" ...

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
WFO.remember("wfo_data/classification.csv") # remember and load as WFO.data
WFO.remember() # in a later session
} # }
